summary: Build the missing finite-area Nielsen cores of finitely generated Fuchsian groups of the second kind, then construct the bordered orbifolds attached to real quadratic narrow ideal classes. Cusp-normalized conformal rigidity recovers the class, while multiplicity-preserving measures and truncated Stokes provide the geometric input to arithmetic equidistribution.

nodes.statement: For a discrete Γ≤PSL₂(ℝ), ΛΓ is the set of ideal-boundary accumulation points of Γz₀, in the closed-disc compactification of ℍ. nodes.title: Nielsen core
nodes.statement: For nonelementary discrete Γ, let CΓ be the intersection of the closed hyperbolic half-planes whose ideal closures contain ΛΓ; equivalently keep the side away from each component interval of the ideal-circle complement. Set NΓ=intℍ(CΓ). The bordered orbifold Core(Γ) is the quotient Γ\CΓ, with quotient topology and the parent’s orbifold charts restricted to the interior. Its genuine boundary is Γ\∂ℍCΓ, not the paired edges of a chosen polygon.
hypotheses: Γ is discrete and nonelementary.
proofSteps: Intersect the supporting closed half-planes; noncollinearity of three limit points gives nonempty interior. Local finiteness of complementary supporting geodesics in ℍ shows that its interior is the open Nielsen region.
Convexity and invariance permit restriction of the orbit relation to CΓ. Away from supporting geodesics use the existing quotient charts; on a supporting line use a half-disc chart.
A nontrivial elliptic stabilizer cannot preserve a supporting half-plane at its boundary point. Boundary charts are therefore ordinary half-discs.

nodes.title: Finite-area Nielsen core
nodes.statement: If Γ≤PSL₂(ℝ) is discrete, nonelementary and finitely generated, it admits a locally finite finite-sided convex fundamental polygon. Its intersection with CΓ has finite area and becomes compact after removing finitely many disjoint cusp horodiscs. There are finitely many Γ-orbits of complementary ideal intervals. Each interval stabilizer is generated by a primitive hyperbolic element, and its supporting geodesic gives one embedded boundary circle. Thus second kind is equivalent to having at least one funnel; for first kind this recovers the parent’s cofinite case.
hypotheses: Γ is discrete, nonelementary and finitely generated; torsion is permitted.
proofSteps: Take a compact regular neighborhood of finitely many generator loops in the quotient, using local orbifold charts; its compactness meets only finitely many cone orbits. Exhaust the remaining quotient by compact subsurfaces and use the inherited van Kampen presentation. After filling inessential boundary discs, a new handle, nonannular end or unaccounted cone introduces a generator not in the original surjective subgroup. The finite generator set therefore forces finite topological type; finite cone data is a conclusion of this argument, not an initial assumption. This is the two-dimensional geometric-finiteness argument summarized by LU23 §3.1.

Cut the resulting finite-type quotient along finitely many arcs to a finite-sided convex polygon; parabolic peripheral loops give cusp vertices, hyperbolic peripheral loops give free ideal intervals. Equivalently use the finite-generation/geometric-finiteness result in LU23 §3.1.

Replace each free interval by its supporting axis. Polygon Gauss–Bonnet gives finite core area. The inherited cusp horodiscs leave a compact polygon. Local separation and discreteness make a boundary-axis stabilizer cyclic with a primitive generator.

sources.match: Finite generation, finite-sided polygons and finite-area Nielsen intersections are the key input, with cusp surgery described in §3.2. The surgery discussions in §3.2–§3.3 first treat torsion-free groups; here cusp isolation comes from F.3 and the cone points remain in the compact part using F.1, so no torsion-free hypothesis is silently dropped.

nodes.title: Primitive funnel boundary
nodes.statement: Each funnel peripheral free homotopy class of the regular part of Core(Γ) has one oriented closed geodesic representative, obtained from the supporting axis of the primitive interval stabilizer. It is simple on Core(Γ), avoids cone points, and is traversed once. Parabolic cusp classes have no such representative. For general hyperbolic conjugacy classes uniqueness is asserted in the orbifold sense; no claim is made that a representative must avoid all cone points.
hypotheses: Γ is discrete, nonelementary and finitely generated. The peripheral class belongs to a funnel, not to a cusp or cone meridian.
proofSteps: Lift the peripheral loop to a path joining z to hz, where h is the primitive hyperbolic stabilizer of its complementary interval.
The two fixed endpoints determine the unique invariant axis. A second geodesic in that class lifts to the same axis by uniqueness of a hyperbolic element’s axis.
Supporting lines are disjoint and boundary stabilizers are cyclic without elliptics; hence the quotient boundary circle is simple. A parabolic element has only one ideal fixed point and no axis.

nodes.title: Cycle polygon presentation
nodes.statement: For an admissible digit list, the Γ(n)-translates of P(n) tile ℍ with disjoint interiors, locally finitely away from ideal endpoints. Boundary identifications are exactly the specified side pairings. The resulting group is ℤ*(C₂)^*ℓ, where T^m generates ℤ and S₀,…,Sℓ₋₁ generate the order-two factors. The quotient has one cusp class and its full stabilizer at ∞ is ⟨T^m⟩; the elliptic orbits are represented once by Nₖ+i, k=0,…,ℓ−1, all of order two. Its underlying topological type is genus zero with one funnel end.
hypotheses: The list is admissible; no assertion of minimality as an arithmetic period is needed for this theorem.
proofSteps: Discreteness is inherited from PSL₂(ℤ). Translate any point into the strip. If it is inside one of the unit discs, apply its involution to increase height; only finitely many integral bottom rows can give height above the original height, so this reduction terminates at P.

For uniqueness, a reduced alternating word in the translation and involution factors carries an interior point into an excluded disc or an exterior strip. This is the disjoint-disc ping-pong argument; it also proves there are no extra relations.

Apply the inherited polygon cycle/orientation bookkeeping to the split half-sides. The only ideal parabolic vertex cycle is ∞, with primitive pairing T^m; traversing the remaining free ideal intervals through their endpoint identifications gives one end circle. The resulting planar polygon gluing gives genus zero.
The reduction normal form shows that an element fixing ∞ has no involution syllable, hence is T^{jm}. It also identifies the ℓ elliptic conjugacy classes.

nodes.title: Boundary word and endpoint ordering
nodes.statement: For a primitive reduced period of A and reduced w>wσ, γ_w=S₁⋯SℓT^m=∏ₖ(T^nₖS) in PSL₂(ℤ). This is the primitive hyperbolic Pell automorph with attracting fixed point w. Set w₁=w and wₖ=Sₖ₋₁⋯S₁w for k≥2, and similarly for the conjugate. Then Nₖ₋₁<wₖσ<Nₖ₋₁+1≤Nₖ−1<wₖ<Nₖ for 1≤k≤ℓ. The weak central inequality permits nₖ=2; all other inequalities are strict.
hypotheses: D>1 is positive fundamental; A∈Cl⁺(K); n is its primitive reduced minus period; ε_D is the least unit >1 of norm +1.
proofSteps: Telescope the conjugation powers in S₁⋯SℓT^m to obtain ∏T^nₖS.
Write each transformed wₖ as Nₖ₋₁ plus its reduced remainder. Reducedness 0<remainderσ<1 and nₖ−1<remainder<nₖ gives the inequalities.

The imported continued-fraction product and Pell dictionary identify the word with multiplication by ε_D, including the attracting direction. A nonprimitive repeated period would give a positive power and is excluded.

sources.match: The source states the matrix word, the transformed endpoint inequalities and closing identity.

acceptance: The all-2 parabolic word fails the strict hyperbolic hypothesis.

nodes.title: Infinite-index cycle subgroup
nodes.statement: For an admissible digit list, Γ(n) is nonelementary, finitely generated, of the second kind and of infinite index in PSL₂(ℤ). Its full upper-half-plane quotient has infinite area although its Nielsen core has finite area. Every nonempty Iₖ from the Ford polygon lies in the domain of discontinuity, so it supplies a concrete ideal point outside the limit set.
hypotheses: All digit assumptions of cycle-polygon hold.
proofSteps: The group contains a nontrivial translation and an involution moving ∞, so its limit set has more than two points.
Ping-pong and the free-side tiling give a neighborhood of each interior point of Iₖ with properly discontinuous action; hence Iₖ misses ΛΓ. Some Iₖ is nonempty.

A positive-length subinterval of Iₖ has a shallow strip in P with area integral ∫y⁻²dy=∞. Thus the quotient has infinite area. A finite-index subgroup of the modular group has finite area by the imported fundamental-domain index formula, proving infinite index.

nodes.title: Boundary arc cutting
nodes.statement: For the data in word-endpoints, let z be the unique intersection of the axis (wσ,w) with |ζ|=1. Cut the oriented finite arc [z,γ_wz] at the next circle |ζ−N₁|=1, retain its initial piece in P and apply S₁ to the remaining piece. Repeat at centers N₂,…,Nℓ. After Sℓ and translation T^−m the endpoint returns to z. The retained arcs form one oriented closed curve in Γ_A\P, lying on supporting geodesics and with the core on its left.
hypotheses: The period is primitive and reduced. Arc order is from wσ towards w; disc tangencies occur only on the real boundary.
proofSteps: The endpoint inequalities give unique crossings of the complete transformed axes with the relevant circles. To justify crossings of the finite subarcs, put qₖ=Sₖ⋯SℓT^m z. Since SℓT^m z=T^mSz and |z|=1, qℓ lies on the final circle.

The identity |Sₖζ−Nₖ|=1/|ζ−Nₖ| and disjoint open discs show by descending induction that qₖ lies strictly inside the circle centered at Nₖ for k<ℓ. The starting point of that cutting step lies outside it. Thus each finite subarc reaches its next circle exactly once; for ℓ=1 the last crossing is the endpoint itself.

Side pairings identify the retained endpoints and tangent directions. Their cyclic order follows the free-end circle of the polygon; their supporting half-planes are the ones containing the limit set. No nontrivial subcycle closes, by the primitive boundary word and normal form.

nodes.title: Quadratic-class surface
nodes.statement: For a real quadratic field K of positive fundamental discriminant D>1 and A∈Cl⁺(K), define F_A=Core(Γ_A), including its genuine geodesic boundary and all cone points with order. A fundamental core polygon is Q_A=P(n)∩CΓ_A. The canonical map p_A:F_A→M=PSL₂(ℤ)\ℍ is induced by subgroup inclusion; it is an orientation-preserving local orbifold isometry on the interior and an isometric half-disc map along the genuine boundary. It may overlap itself and is proper. Choices of reduced representative produce canonically conjugate maps over M.
hypotheses: Use a primitive minus period supplied by GN.3; all arithmetic actions and the modular quotient use the effective projective group.
proofSteps: Apply the general core construction to the explicit second-kind subgroup, restricting the actual orbit relation and quotient charts.

Identify Q_A by the supporting retained arcs from axis-cutting. Choose Y₀>1 above all those finitely many compact arcs. Above Y₀ the core polygon is the full width-m cusp strip. The cutoff 1 works for P(n), but need not work for Q_A.

Inclusion of orbit relations gives p_A. Above a sufficiently high standard modular horodisc it is the width-m cusp cover; the complement of that cusp tail in F_A is compact. This proves properness, hence finiteness of preimages away from the projected boundary and cone set.
Use rotation-conjugacy for independence; do not replace the surface by a record of signature, area and length.

proofSteps: The Ford gluing supplies genus zero, the ℓ distinct cone orbits, and the unique cusp and free-end cycle.

For every modular-invariant continuous one-form whose restriction to this compact cycle is integrable, its integral along ∂F_A equals the imported oriented integral along C_A. No division by two is made for a reciprocal class A²=J, although its modular image may retrace.
hypotheses: Use the primitive Pell generator attracting w, and orient ∂F_A with the core on its left. ε_D is the least norm +1 unit >1.
proofSteps: The retained pieces are images of a partition of [z,γ_wz], each by an orientation-preserving isometry belonging to the full modular group.
Sum lengths and one-form integrals over the partition. The imported GN.4 length theorem applies to the whole primitive parametrized cycle.

It is strictly increasing. These are distances of specified lifts in ℍ; they are not asserted to be distances of the corresponding cone points in F_A.

nodes.title: Double of a bordered core
nodes.statement: For a finite-area Nielsen core with t≥1 geodesic boundary circles, glue it to a second copy with conjugate complex structure along the identical boundary points. The double is an oriented complete boundaryless hyperbolic orbifold with genus 2g+t−1, twice the cone-order multiset, 2s cusps and area twice the core area. Reflection interchanges the two copies. It has orbifold universal cover ℍ, obtained by reflecting its cut polygon across the genuine geodesic boundary sides.
hypotheses: The core is connected, nonelementary and geometrically finite; each genuine boundary component is a smooth closed geodesic without cone points.
proofSteps: Use half-disc charts along the boundary and the conjugate chart on the second copy. Geodesic reflection glues them analytically and isometrically; existing interior cone charts remain unchanged.
Double a finite cut polygon. The inherited polygon theorem and reflected side identifications give the boundaryless orbifold quotient of ℍ; cusp ends stay complete.
Compute Euler characteristic by gluing along t circles, each of Euler characteristic zero. Count the two copies of each cusp and cone orbit and compare area by integration.

nodes.title: Conformal orbifold conjugacy
nodes.statement: An orientation-preserving conformal orbifold equivalence f:Core(Γ_A)→Core(Γ_B), continuous and bijective on their genuine boundaries, is a hyperbolic isometry. It lifts to φ∈PSL₂(ℝ) with φΓ_Aφ⁻¹=Γ_B and φCΓ_A=CΓ_B. The hypothesis preserves each cone order, not just the coarse conformal structure. After composing φ with an element of Γ_B, the unique cusp condition gives φ(∞)=∞, hence φ(z)=az+b for a>0 and b∈ℝ.
hypotheses: A and B belong to the same fixed real quadratic field. The equivalence is holomorphic on the interior in orbifold charts and preserves its orientation and cone orders.
proofSteps: Double f by reflection using the analytic boundary charts. Remove the cone points and apply the pinned ordinary covering lifting criterion to the covers obtained from the reflected polygon groups, after rebasing the target cover by the doubled f. These punctured surfaces and covering spaces are path connected and locally path connected; choose matching lifted basepoints.

The subgroup defining the orbifold universal cover is the normal closure of the mⱼth powers of small cone meridians. Cone-order preservation carries this subgroup to the matching subgroup, so the lift exists in both directions. Local maps extend across removed lifts by the removable-singularity theorem in disc coordinates.

Choose matching lifted basepoints in the first halves of the doubles. Uniqueness of based lifts makes the two chosen lifts inverse and supplies deck equivariance; the pinned deck conjugation API packages the resulting cover isomorphism. The inverse lifts extend to a biholomorphism ℍ→ℍ; by the imported disc automorphism/Schwarz–Pick equality classification it is a PSL₂(ℝ) isometry. The corresponding connected preimage halves are the convex, hence simply connected, cores CΓ_A and CΓ_B; their stabilizers in the doubled polygon groups are exactly the original Γ_A and Γ_B. Thus the lift maps these halves onto each other and conjugates their stabilizers. This proves the required core-group conjugacy, not only conjugacy of the larger doubled groups.
Conjugacy sends parabolics and their fixed points to parabolics. Since Γ_B has one cusp orbit, compose by its deck element to fix ∞. The real projective normal form is az+b with positive a.

nodes.title: Highest elliptic lifts
nodes.statement: For Γ(n), the union of all elliptic fixed points has maximal imaginary part 1, and the points attaining it are exactly {Nₖ+jm+i:0≤k<ℓ,j∈ℤ}. More precisely for γ represented by [[a,b],[c,d]] and Pₖ=Nₖ+i, Im(γPₖ)=1/((cNₖ+d)²+c²)≤1; equality holds exactly when γ∈⟨T^m⟩ or γ∈⟨T^m⟩Sₖ. The full stabilizer and the complete list of elliptic orbits are necessary inputs.
hypotheses: n is admissible; matrix entries are integral and determinant one; Sₖ and γ are interpreted projectively.
γ belongs to Γ(n), and 0≤k<ℓ. The equality classification is not asserted for arbitrary ambient modular matrices.
proofSteps: Apply the pinned imaginary-part formula at Pₖ. The denominator is a positive integer, so it is at least one.
Equality of the sum of two integer squares to one leaves (c,d)=±(0,1) or c=±1,d=−cNₖ. In the first case γ is a translation; in the second γSₖ is a translation.
Use the full cusp stabilizer ⟨T^m⟩, not the ambient modular translation group, to identify the exact maximal-height points. Apply the orbit classification from ford-domain to include all elliptics.

nodes.title: Conformal class determines the ideal class
nodes.statement: For A,B∈Cl⁺(K) in a fixed real quadratic field, there is an orientation-preserving conformal equivalence of bordered orbifolds F_A≅F_B if and only if A=B. It is sufficient to retain the cone points and their orders, the cusp and the oriented bordered conformal structure; the projection to M is not part of the required invariant.
hypotheses: The reduced periods used to construct F_A,F_B are primitive. Conformal equivalence has the precise meaning in conformal-lift.
proofSteps: Normalize its lift as φ(z)=az+b. Since φ bijects the entire elliptic fixed-point sets and scales their heights, the maximum-height theorem gives a=1.
The full positive cusp translation period therefore agrees: m_A=m_B. Translation by b carries the cyclic ordered sets of height-one lifts modulo m onto one another.

Their positive successive gaps are the digit cycles, up to cyclic rotation. Apply the imported complete-invariant theorem of GN.3 to conclude A=B. Conversely equal classes have rotated reduced periods and rotation-conjugacy supplies the equivalence.

Use the parent’s modular quotient and its measure μ_mod of total mass π/3; this adapter introduces no new modular fundamental-domain theorem.

nodes.title: Complementary class surfaces
nodes.statement: Let J be the narrow class of the different, J²=1, and let ι(A)=JA⁻¹. Then ν_A+ν_{ι(A)}=3(ℓ_A+ℓ_{ι(A)})μ_mod. Equivalently the combined local sheet count is the indicated integer almost everywhere. The projected oriented boundaries agree with opposite parametrizations. This statement includes A=ι(A), reciprocal projected geodesics and repeated or crossing arcs.
hypotheses: D>1 is positive fundamental; ν_A is the multiplicity-preserving pushforward and μ_mod has mass π/3.
proofSteps: Import the oriented geodesic-reversal identity from GN.4 and the full once-traversed boundary identification from N.2/boundary-length. Thus the pushed-forward oriented boundary arcs cancel with signed multiplicity, even when their images retrace.

By properness and the local isometry charts, each ν has a finite integer local density on the regular modular surface away from the locally finite projected boundary. It is constant on each chamber; crossing an oriented smooth boundary arc changes it by its signed number of preimages.

Opposite parametrized boundary arcs make all jumps of the sum zero. The regular modular surface is connected, so the sum density is one constant almost everywhere.

nodes.title: Exact genus covering
nodes.statement: If a nonempty finite family S is stable under ι(A)=JA⁻¹, then Σ_{A∈S}ν_A=3(Σ_{A∈S}ℓ_A)μ_mod and ρ_S=μ_prob. The imported arithmetic criterion says J is a square exactly when no prime p≡3 mod 4 divides D, equivalently D is a sum of two integer squares. The latter criterion is not the stronger assertion J=1 or existence of a negative-norm unit.
hypotheses: Use the same fundamental discriminant and narrow group as the supplier. A genus is a coset of the square subgroup.
proofSteps: Sum complementarity over S. The involution permutes S, so the left sum is twice Σν_A and the length sum is twice Σℓ_A; divide the finite real measure identity by two.

In the exponent-two genus quotient inversion is the identity, and multiplication by J preserves each coset exactly when J is a square. Apply the imported RQ.2 criterion without reproving genus theory.
For A²=J, ι fixes A and complementarity directly gives ν_A=3ℓ_Aμ_mod. Divide by the positive total mass for probability normalization.

nodes.title: Cusp-truncated core
nodes.statement: Choose Y>1 above every finite boundary arc of Q_A and put Q_A(Y)=Q_A∩{Im z≤Y}. It is a compact piecewise smooth region with top segment 0≤x≤m at height Y. With the orientation dx∧dy, this segment is traversed from m+iY to iY. Its remaining edges consist of the true positively oriented core boundary and oppositely paired polygon sides. For C² F invariant under Γ_A, set α_F=i∂zF dz, with ∂zF=(F_x−iF_y)/2. It is an invariant one-form; it is not the real exterior derivative of F.
hypotheses: F is complex-valued and C² in real coordinates; side pairings are holomorphic, and genuine boundary orientation has the core on its left.
proofSteps: The explicit core polygon has a full width-m strip above its finite boundary arcs. Intersect with the height half-plane to get a compact finite-corner region.
Orient each edge as a boundary of the planar region. Paired sides cancel after pullback by their holomorphic isometries; the horizontal top has the stated right-to-left direction.
For cone vertices use their order-two local covers, or excise small discs and let their radii tend to zero. C¹ boundedness near lifts makes the extra integrals vanish.

nodes.title: Nielsen-core Stokes formula
nodes.statement: Let F:ℍ→ℂ be C², Γ_A-invariant and satisfy ΔF=−y²(F_xx+F_yy)=λF with λ∈ℂ. Assume ∫₀ᵐ∂zF(x+iY)dx→0 as Y→∞. Then I_A(F)=lim_{Y→∞}∫_{Q_A(Y)}F dμ exists as a finite complex number and (λ/2)I_A(F)=∮_{∂F_A}i∂zF dz. When F is μ_A-integrable this limit is its ordinary integral. No absolute integrability is claimed solely from the flux hypothesis. If F is invariant under the full modular group, the right side is the integral along the complete parametrized C_A.
hypotheses: The differential operator is curvature −1 with the minus sign and factor y². The complex-valued integral is in the orientation of N.2.
proofSteps: In real coordinates d(i∂zF dz)=−(F_xx+F_yy)dx∧dy/2=(λ/2)F dμ. Apply imported ordinary/corners Stokes to the real and imaginary parts on Q_A(Y), multiplying by a smooth cutoff equal to one on a neighborhood of this compact polygon to meet the supplier’s compact-support hypothesis; the one-form is C¹ and all side/cone cancellations are given by core-truncation.
The exact finite identity is (λ/2)∫_{Q_A(Y)}F dμ=∮_{∂F_A}α_F−i∫₀ᵐ∂zF(x+iY)dx. For λ≠0 the assumed flux convergence gives existence and the limit formula.

For λ=0, write a(Y)=∫₀ᵐF(x+iY)dx. Translation periodicity and the harmonic equation give a″=0; integrating F_x over a period gives zero, so the flux is −ia′/2. Its limit zero forces a′=0, and the tail integral ∫a(Y)Y⁻²dY converges. Thus the height-truncated integral exists in this case as well.

For L¹ functions use exhaustion/dominated convergence to compare with the measure integral. Γ_A-invariance already permits all the cutting maps Sₖ and T^m, so boundaryCut_isometry identifies the boundary integral with the integral on the selected axis segment in ℍ. Full modular invariance is needed to descend the form to M and interpret this intrinsically as an integral along the complete parametrized modular cycle C_A.

sources.match: The source proves the flux-to-boundary identity. The plan specifies its improper interpretation and separately proves existence when λ=0.

acceptance: The coefficient is λ/2, not λ or λ/(2i).
For F=1 and λ=0 both sides vanish while I_A(1)=πℓ_A.
No division by λ occurs in the harmonic branch.

nodes.title: Automorphic surface-to-cycle identity
nodes.statement: For a smooth level-one weight-zero Maass cusp eigenfunction u with eigenvalue λ, and for the completed weight-zero Eisenstein function E*(z,1/2+it) of AS.1–AS.2 with t∈ℝ, both the L¹ core integral and the horizontal flux condition hold. For each such F, (λ_F/2)∫_{F_A}F dμ=∫_{C_A}i∂zF dz, where λ_E=1/4+t² and λ_u is the given cusp eigenvalue. At t=0 take the regular holomorphic value of the completed Eisenstein function, with cancellation between its two constant terms. This endpoint is not defined by evaluating two separate pole terms.
hypotheses: Use the AS completion E*=Λ(2s)E, including its half-sum normalization, continuation and poles only at s=0,1. Cusp forms have zero horizontal Fourier constant term.
proofSteps: Import the AS Fourier expansions and the differentiated cusp estimates requested below. Nonzero Fourier modes and their first derivatives decay exponentially on high strips, and integrating over the integer width m kills them exactly.

For cusp forms the horizontal mean is zero. For E* on Re s=1/2 its constant term is O(√Y log Y), including the removable t=0 cancellation, and its derivative is O(Y⁻¹/² log Y). Therefore the horizontal flux tends to zero.
The same growth makes |F|Y⁻² integrable over the width-m cusp strip; compact remainder integrability follows from smoothness and finite orbifold charts.
Apply core-stokes and full modular invariance. No Hecke normalization, parity, subconvexity or asymptotic equidistribution proof is added here.
